clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with a 5-month progressive course of cognitive decline, behavioral disturbances, insomnia, visual hallucinations, myoclonus, and characteristic faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS occurring 30-50 times daily, brief 5-second episodes, stress-triggered, involving arm, ipsilateral face, and occasionally ipsilateral leg). On admission, he was confused, drowsy, disoriented in time and place with marked short-term memory impairment (MMSE 15/30). Neurological examination revealed asymmetric akinetic-rigid syndrome and bilateral palmomental reflexes. Prior medical history included vitiligo (2 years prior), verruca seborrhoica, GERD, and recently diagnosed diabetes requiring insulin. Diagnostic workup revealed: (1) high-titer serum VGKC-complex antibodies (678.3 pmol/L, positive >85 pmol/L) with LGI1 as the specific antigenic target and negative CASPR2 antibodies, confirming autoimmune limbic encephalitis; (2) brain MRI with no hippocampal lesions; (3) CSF with elevated protein (0.91 g/L) but normal white cell count; (4) EEG showing disorganization and slowing of background activity without periodic synchronous discharges. The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days). After 1 month, he became seizure-free with significant cognitive improvement (MMSE 27/30). He remained under regular follow-up for 18 months with no relapse, and antiepileptic treatment was progressively diminished. Incidental imaging findings revealed intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasia (IPMN) of the pancreas with no signs of malignancy.

EEG findings of disorganization and slowing of background activity without periodic discharges consistent with encephalitis
